hints: Look at what n − 1 does to the binary form of n: which bits change? Now combine n and n − 1 with AND.
Use Brian Kernighan's trick: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit. Repeat until n is 0 and count the steps; the loop runs once per 1-bit.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Check all 32 bit positions with (n >> i) & 1 and add them up.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Clear the lowest set bit with n & (n − 1) until n becomes 0; iterations = number of ones.

explain: Sample 13 = 1101. Step 1: 13 & 12 = 1101 & 1100 = 1100 (12). Step 2: 12 & 11 = 1100 & 1011 = 1000 (8). Step 3: 8 & 7 = 0. Three steps, so the answer is 3. It works because subtracting 1 flips the lowest 1 to 0 and all the 0s below it to 1, so the AND wipes exactly that lowest 1. Edge case: n = 0 returns 0 without entering the loop.
recognize: 'How many 1s in the binary form' → bit tricks: n & (n − 1) removes one set bit per step.
